Pittsburgh Panthers football team|1979]], [[1980 Pittsburgh Panthers football team|1980]]) | awards = }} '''Tim Lewis''' (born December 18, 1961) is an American [[American football|football]] coach and former player who was most recently the [[defensive coordinator]] for the [[Boston College Eagles football|Boston College Eagles]]. He played [[college football]] as a [[cornerback]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]] and was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in the first round of the [[1983 NFL draft]]. Following a neck injury that cut his playing career short after four seasons, Lewis began serving as a coach in the collegiate and professional levels and obtained his first head coaching position with the [[Birmingham Iron]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]] (AAF) in 2019. He also served as the defensive backs coach for the [[St. Louis BattleHawks]] and co-defensive coordinator for the [[Arlington Renegades]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]]. Lewis is the younger brother of former [[Memphis Express]] General Manager Will Lewis. [[Louis Riddick]], former NFL safety and current ESPN broadcaster, is his cousin. [[Robb Riddick]], another of his cousins, was a running back for the [[Buffalo Bills]] for eight seasons.

'''Timothy Thomas McTyer''' (born December 14, 1975) is the head [[American football]] coach at [[Adelanto High School]] in California and a former [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played two seasons for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and one for the [[Cleveland Browns]].  He played [[college football]] at [[Brigham Young University]]. He was hired as head football coach of [[Phineas Banning High School|Banning High School]] in February 2010 after coaching at local high schools and [[Los Angeles Southwest College]]. '''Timote Taliai Manoa''' (born September 9, 1964) is a Tongan-born former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] for four seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Cleveland Browns]] and  [[Indianapolis Colts]]. He played collegiately at [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]] and was a member of both the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football under Joe Paterno (as an Independent)#1986 season|1986]] national championship team.
Manoa was born in Tonga, but at age 10 moved to [[Hawaii]] where he discovered American football.<ref name="vanfossaninterview">{{cite news | url = http://www.clevelandleader.com/node/10226 | title = Interview with former Penn State Nittany Lion and Cleveland Browns' fullback Tim Manoa | newspaper = [[The Plain Dealer|Cleveland Leader]] | last = VanFossan | first = Brad | date = 2009-06-09 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20100312014628/http://www.clevelandleader.com/node/10226 | archivedate = 2010-03-12 }}</ref> He attended [[Kahuku High & Intermediate School|Kahuku High School]] from grades 7 to 9 before moving to [[Wexford, Pennsylvania]]. There he attended [[North Allegheny Senior High School|North Allegheny High]]
.<ref name="vanfossaninterview"/> Manoa was named a Parade [[All-America]]n<ref name="psumediaguide">{{cite book | title = Penn State 1986 Season: A Century of Excellence, 1887-1986 | publisher = Penn State University Department of Sport Information | page = 25 | year = 1986}}</ref> and was heavily recruited by several top college football programs, including [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]], [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pitt]], [[Hawaii Warriors football|Hawaii]], and [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State]], before selecting Penn State.<ref name="vanfossaninterview"/>

After outstanding junior and senior seasons as part of Penn State's "Baby Bull Backfield" fullback tandem (with [[Steve Smith (running back)|Steve Smith]]),<ref name="psumediaguide"/> Manoa was invited to the [[Hula Bowl]], [[Senior Bowl]], and the [[NFL Combine]]<ref name="vanfossaninterview"/> where his NFL draft stock rose steadily. He was selected in the 3rd round (#80) of the [[1987 NFL draft]] by the Browns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=2023-09-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He would play 3 seasons in Cleveland under [[Marty Schottenheimer]] and [[Bud Carson]] before moving on for a final season with Indianapolis.

Manoa now teaches speed training at Rocky's Personalized Training in [[Boardman, Ohio]].<ref name="vanfossaninterview"/>
